evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/realtor/[id]/page.tsx:11-20 — the public agent-profile page for the dynamic route /[locale]/realtor/[id] imports MOCK_AGENT, MOCK_AGENT_LISTINGS, MOCK_AGENT_REVIEWS from ./_mock (:11) and binds `const agent = MOCK_AGENT` (:20). The component signature is `export default function AgentProfilePage()` with NO props and it never reads the `[id]` route param (no `params`, no `useParams`): confirmed by grep — the only `params` occurrence in the file is the `/[locale]/realtor/[id]` route string in the header comment. Consequently EVERY agent URL (`/sk/realtor/anything`, `/sk/realtor/<real-uuid>`, etc.) renders the exact same hard-coded fake agent, fake listing grid (:227 `MOCK_AGENT_LISTINGS.length`, :237 `.map`), and fake reviews (:330 `MOCK_AGENT_REVIEWS.length`, :333 `.map`) on a public, SEO-indexed portal route. This is the SAME defect class the sibling page frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/profile/page.tsx:12-15 documents it already fixed — its header comment says it 'previously rendered a shared MOCK_PROFILE ("Tomas Novotny") to every visitor, which was both a UX bug and a privacy footgun' — so the repo already treats shared-mock-to-every-visitor as a real bug, and realtor/[id] is the un-migrated twin. The backing APIs partly exist in frontend/apps/reality-web/src/lib/realtor-api.ts: reviews are available via getRealtorReviews(realtorId) (:233 → GET /api/v1/realtors/{id}/reviews) and the authenticated profile via getMyRealtorProfile (:67); the fix needs those plus a public realtor-by-id profile GET (realtor-api.ts currently only exposes the `/me` profile, so a public `GET /api/v1/realtors/{id}` may need adding/confirming server-side). NET-NEW vs backlog: the only existing reality-web/realtor row is bug-reality-web-realtor-invite-silent-error (RealtorManagement.tsx invite flow — a different file and feature); nothing covers the realtor/[id] public profile stub. Severity MEDIUM (+2): user-facing wrong data on every public agent page, not a crash/auth bypass. Confidence HIGH: statically certain — the page imports only mocks and never touches the route param or any fetch. Cloud-landable (reality-web Next.js, CI + vitest verifiable).

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/realtor/[id]/page.tsx:22-27 — the 'Contact agent' form submit handler `handleSendMessage` is purely local: `if (message.trim()) { setMessageSent(true); setContactOpen(false); }`. It performs NO network call — no fetch, no realtor-api helper, no mutation (confirmed: the file's only imports are `useState` from react and the MOCK_* consts; there is no inquiry/contact API call anywhere in the file). The form at :591 (`onSubmit={handleSendMessage}`) therefore shows the user a success state (`messageSent`) while silently dropping the message: the agent never receives any inquiry. This is a silent-data-loss UX bug on a public lead-capture surface — a prospective buyer believes they contacted the agent but nothing was sent. Distinct work item from the shared-mock finding (that one wires GET profile/reviews data; this one needs an inquiry/contact POST endpoint wired to submit). NET-NEW vs backlog: no existing row covers the realtor/[id] contact form. Severity MEDIUM (+2): user-facing action silently no-ops (lost leads). Confidence HIGH: statically certain the handler never leaves local component state. Cloud-landable (reality-web, vitest-verifiable with a mocked submit).
